case: MySQL ENUM and SET parser/keyed edit across SQL modes
contract: Grid parsing validates values against the declared ENUM/SET members, including apostrophe and backslash metadata, and refuses unknown labels or members.

Bound keyed edits preserve ENUM label bytes and a multi-member SET mask under eight modes: default, NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, ANSI_QUOTES, their combination, STRICT_TRANS_TABLES and STRICT_ALL_TABLES, each strict mode with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES.
Blank input retains shared SQL NULL/required-field behavior, while explicit `''` selects an empty ENUM label or the empty SET value; native ordinals/masks distinguish empty values from NULL.
The native server control demonstrates that permissive mode otherwise coerces an unknown ENUM label to its error value and drops an unknown SET member; the control updates are rolled back.
An untouched sibling row retains its native ordinals, masks and label bytes in every mode.
The literal label `NULL` is accepted as a non-NULL ENUM value on both engines; its ordinal and bytes are checked separately from the SQL NULL row.

MariaDB 11 reports the declared ENUM/SET members in column metadata; valid apostrophe/backslash values bind and retain their native ordinals, masks and bytes in all eight modes, while invalid labels and members are refused.
